title: Healthleap banks $38M for AI screening platform that catches undiagnosed conditions
source_used: TechCrunch (exclusive of 7 Oct 2026; Fierce Healthcare page blocked)
key_facts: Healthleap raised $38 million in seed and Series A funding, TechCrunch learned exclusively: an $8m seed co-led by Sequoia Capital and First Round Capital and a $30m Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures.
Founded in South Africa in 2022 by siblings Jemima and Josiah Meyer.

The platform plugs into hospital electronic health records, uses language models to read clinicians' written notes and, with labs and vital signs, writes a risk score each morning for conditions such as malnutrition and delirium.
It is deployed in more than 50 hospitals, up from three a year ago; customers include Penn Medicine, Cedars-Sinai, Intermountain, Houston Methodist and Emory Healthcare.
The company says its software does not diagnose patients, only highlights items for review.
The company says its malnutrition programme produced $23.8m in annualised financial impact at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania (self-reported).
quote_evidence: The company notes that its software doesn't diagnose patients, only highlights items for additional review.

Josiah said Healthleap has grown from three hospital partners to more than 50 over the past year, and its customers now include Penn Medicine, Cedars-Sinai, Intermountain, Houston Methodist, and Emory Healthcare.
why_it_matters_hint: Tests whether AI reading chart notes can catch under-diagnosed hospital conditions.
notes: Funding announced 7 Oct (TechCrunch); Fierce followed 8 Oct. Score lowered by 1 as event is before 8 Oct. ROI figures are company claims.
